text:
I did giyur via ITIM, they are amazing and helpful. 

They did not accept people on B1 visa, but I started the process and lessons right after I got A5. 

I did a research before and I trully believe there is no orthodox private conversion that allows you to start on B1, at least the ones recognized by the state. Also you need to have a chuppah after you complete the giyur which requires a civil marriage from abroad dobe before. (Which sounds strange, but this is how it is...)

They are modern orthodox, so in many things they are more relaxed, nobody forces you to wear muted colours and shirts, but of course you have to be dressed modestly. For example, as a woman you can wear trousers, as long as they are not tight. But halacha still applies, as in all.

We don't have a childern, but if you have a childern under the age of bar/bat mitzva, they can do it with you. 

Only cons is propably that as any other giyur done by private beit din, you are not recognized by the rabanut because rabanut recognizes only their conversions (done in Israel).

But after the process you can apply for a status change in misrad hapnim to "jewish", of course you pay for it. It should take around half year to finish. If you apply as a family, the costs of the lawyer are same as one person. I am now in this stage, so I cannot tell you more about this.

I am happy to answer any other questions.
